group: insects: Pheidole big-headed ants (Friedman et al. 2019: 651 minor heads, 502 major heads [23 LMs], minor & major mesosomas [10 LMs] across ~200 species on Pheidole_Tree.phy)

data.landmarks: Friedman NR, Bennett BL, Fischer G, Sarnat EM, Huang JP, Knowles LL, Economo EP 2020 Syst Biol / Dryad (Zenodo 5096592): 23-LM head shape (`Aligned_Head_Minor.TPS`, `Aligned_Head_Major.TPS`) and 10-LM mesosoma profile (`Pheidole_minors_Mesosoma.tps`, `Pheidole_majors_Mesosoma.tps`), mapped via `Pheidole_Morphology_Data_03282019.csv`.
data.phylogeny: Time-calibrated phylogeny `Pheidole_Tree.phy` (447 tips; ~200 matched species with landmark data).

what_thompson_specifically_adds: Provides a direct independent replication of our Camponotus carpenter-ant caste discovery in the most famously dimorphic ant genus on Earth (*Pheidole*, which Thompson himself cited on p. 732 for the ovate-to-cordate soldier head transformation!). Tests whether within-species minor -> major soldier polyphenism and between-species radiation follow the 7 Thompson modes across ~200 species.

hypotheses.statement: Between-species 23-LM head shape in both minor workers and major soldiers is strongly Thompsonian: Thompson-7 captures > 60% of interspecific Procrustes variance across the ~200 Pheidole species.
hypotheses.reasoning: In Camponotus (82 LMs), Thompson-7 captured 81.2% of interspecific frontal-head variance; Pheidole's 23 head landmarks trace the same continuous bilobed occipital/lateral capsule plus eye/mandible anchors.

hypotheses.statement: Within-species minor -> major soldier caste transformation vectors on the 23-LM head are well-captured by Thompson's 7 global coordinate modes (> 55% of pooled caste-shift variance).
hypotheses.reasoning: Soldier head hypertrophy in Pheidole is the textbook juvenile-hormone growth gradient (ovate minor -> cordate/bilobed major occipital expansion).

hypotheses.statement: Developmental channelling (G_caste vs R_species): the principal axis of within-species minor->major caste divergence aligns more strongly with the principal axis of between-species macroevolutionary divergence inside the 7-D Thompson subspace than in the orthogonal non-Thompson residual subspace (|cos theta|_T7 > |cos theta|_res) on the 23-LM head.
hypotheses.reasoning: Direct replication of Hypothesis A7 from Camponotus (where |cos theta|_T7 = 0.903 vs |cos theta|_res = 0.301 on the frontal head).

hypotheses.statement: Leave-one-species-out phylogenetic prediction on `Pheidole_Tree.phy` beats the grand consensus (median Procrustes RMS ratio < 0.95, paired one-sided Wilcoxon p < 0.01) for minor head shape.
hypotheses.reasoning: Resolved molecular phylogeny across ~200 species captures Old World vs New World and clade-level head-shape syndromes.

hypotheses.statement: Interior sensory/oral landmarks (eyes, antennal insertions, clypeus: the 8 landmarks closest to the anterior/interior centroid) have a higher unexplained residual fraction after Thompson-7 than the 15 outer head-capsule contour landmarks.
hypotheses.reasoning: Replicates Hypothesis A8 from Camponotus: the outer head capsule deforms as a smooth continuous shell under Thompson-7, while eye and antennal-socket positions shift locally.
